seoTitle: How to Connect GitHub to Claude AI (2026)
metaDescription: Bring your GitHub repositories into Claude from the + button in chat or a project, see exactly what Claude can read, and manage access afterward.
intro:
Linking GitHub to Claude brings your repositories into a conversation instead of pasting files back and forth. The connection starts from the same + button used to attach anything else to a chat, not a separate settings page, and it only ever pulls file names, file contents and branch content; never commit history, pull requests, issues or other repository metadata.

This guide walks through starting the connection from a chat and from a project, what the GitHub authorization screen grants, and how to keep the content current or revoke access later.
prerequisites: A GitHub account with at least one repository you can access
A Claude.ai account — the GitHub integration is available on every plan, including Free
costNote: Connecting GitHub doesn't require a paid Claude plan. Anthropic's documentation lists the integration as available on all plans, including Free.

steps.heading: Check your GitHub dashboard is ready
steps.body: Before starting the connection, sign in to the GitHub account you want Claude working against. The dashboard's left sidebar lists your top repositories, a quick way to confirm you're in the right account if you manage more than one. You don't need to change anything here. If you work across a personal account and an organization account, decide up front which one you're connecting; switching later means repeating the authorization from GitHub's side.

image.caption: The GitHub dashboard, showing top repositories in the sidebar, worth a glance to confirm you're signed into the right account before connecting.

steps.heading: Start the connection from the + button
steps.body: In Claude, open a chat and click the + button in the lower-left corner of the message box, then choose Add from GitHub. Inside a project instead, click the + button in the project knowledge section and choose GitHub from the dropdown. Either way, that's the whole starting point. There's no separate Connectors page to visit first for a basic connection.

image.caption: Claude's home screen. A new chat's message box carries the + button that starts the GitHub connection, labeled Add from GitHub.

steps.heading: Authorize Claude to access your GitHub account
steps.body: If you aren't already authenticated with GitHub, clicking Add from GitHub redirects you to a GitHub authorization screen headed "Claude by Anthropic wants access to your GitHub account." Read the permission list before continuing; it covers verifying your identity, knowing which resources you can access, and acting on your behalf. Click Authorize and you land back in Claude automatically, inside the file browser.

image.caption: GitHub's authorization screen for Claude, listing exactly what access you're granting before you click Authorize.

steps.heading: Browse and select repositories
steps.body: Search for the repository you want or paste its URL, then use the file browser to pick specific files and folders instead of handing over an entire codebase at once. If a warning appears after you enter a valid private repository URL, follow the link to the GitHub App: grant access yourself, choosing between all repositories or specific ones, or request access, which emails an organization administrator so you can sync once they approve it.

steps.heading: Know what Claude can and can't see
steps.body: The integration syncs a snapshot of the branch you selected. Everything else about a repository's history stays out of reach unless you paste it in yourself.

steps.heading: Keep content current, or revoke access later
steps.body: Once a repository is attached, use the Sync icon to pull its latest commits on that branch, and the Configure files icon to change which files and folders are included. To remove the connection entirely, open Settings, then Customize, then Connectors, where GitHub is listed among your connected integrations. Removing it there, or revoking access from GitHub's own Settings under Applications, both work. Do either one after you've changed which repositories an AI tool should see.

image.caption: Claude's Connectors panel, where a connected GitHub integration is listed for management or removal. This is separate from the + button used to start a new connection.

troubleshooting.problem: A private repository URL comes back with a warning
troubleshooting.cause: Claude doesn't have access yet, the expected behavior for private repositories until you grant it.
troubleshooting.fix: Follow the link to the GitHub App to grant access yourself, or request it. An organization administrator gets an email and approves it from their side.

troubleshooting.cause: The integration only reflects branch content from when it was added or last synced, not live commits.
troubleshooting.fix: Click Sync on the attached repository before asking anything that depends on recent changes.

troubleshooting.problem: Claude can't answer questions about a pull request or issue
troubleshooting.cause: The GitHub integration retrieves file names, file contents and branch content only. Pull requests, issues, commit history and repository metadata aren't pulled in.
troubleshooting.fix: Paste the relevant PR description, issue text or commit message into the chat directly.

faq.question: What can I do once GitHub is connected to Claude?
faq.answer: Claude can read the files and folders you've selected: summarizing code, drafting a pull request description grounded in the real diff, or answering questions about the repository. It can't see commit history, existing pull requests, issues or other metadata unless you paste that in.

faq.question: Where do I start the connection?
faq.answer: Click the + button in a chat's message box and choose Add from GitHub, or the + button in a project's knowledge section and choose GitHub. There's no separate settings page to visit first.

faq.question: What access does the GitHub authorization screen grant?
faq.answer: It's GitHub's own screen, headed "Claude by Anthropic wants access to your GitHub account." It covers verifying your identity, knowing which resources you can access, and acting on your behalf. Review that list before clicking Authorize.

faq.question: Why does Claude say my repository is out of date?
faq.answer: The integration doesn't refresh automatically. Click the Sync icon on the attached repository to pull its latest branch content.

faq.question: How do I disconnect GitHub later?
faq.answer: Remove it from Settings, Customize, Connectors in Claude, or revoke it from GitHub's own Settings under Applications. Either side works.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded in July 2025. The connection's starting point and what content the integration retrieves were re-checked against Claude's official documentation and Help Center article in September 2026. That check corrected the article's claim that the connection starts from a Settings, Connectors page; it now starts from the + button in a chat or project instead.
